commitResults.messageBody:
The Java sources lack consistent documentation, encapsulation, and naming,
which makes the task manager harder to maintain.

- Add Javadocs and override annotations to clarify the task model.
- Replace public mutable state and ambiguous names with private fields,
  constants, and descriptive task variables.
- Print only the updated task after mark or unmark commands.

Keep task behavior unchanged while making status updates clearer.

The project needs local guidance for consistent Java style and Git history management.

- Add project skills for the SE-EDU Java and Git conventions.
- Require those standards in AGENTS.md for future code and commits.

Make the standards discoverable and apply them consistently across the project.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align Claude instructions with project standards
commitResults.messageBody: CLAUDE.md should state the same local requirements as the main agent instructions so all project agents follow one policy.\n\nAdd direct references to the project-specific Java and Git standards.

commitResults.messageTitle: Changed class structure of Task, Todo, and Deadline
Added Event class and changed input handling
Improved input handling to work for Todo, Deadline, and Event classes
Place Java classes in a project package
commitResults.messageBody: The Java classes are in the default package, which makes ownership and imports less explicit as the project grows.\n\nAdd the lower-case drpijon package to every application class. Keep runtime behavior unchanged while making the project structure explicit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace global task storage with a task list
commitResults.messageBody: The command loop stores tasks in a fixed array and tracks the next position through global state. This couples unrelated methods and duplicates manual count updates.\n\nUse a List<Task> so storage and collection size remain together. Let the list provide task indexing and count information, which removes the capacity magic number, global taskCount, and repeated increment logic without changing the user-visible commands.

Event creation reports both endpoints in its confirmation, but the start-time field reads the end-time value. This makes valid event input appear incorrect to the user.\n\nRead the event's from value for the from field so the confirmation reflects the data that was entered.

Deadline and event commands index delimiter parts without checking their presence, so incomplete input can terminate the application with an exception.\n\nValidate the required sections before constructing structured tasks and reuse a named invalid-input message. Keep valid commands unchanged while making malformed input fail safely.

Event is a public task type but provides no class or constructor documentation, which makes its time-range semantics less clear to maintainers.\n\nAdd concise Javadocs describing the event model and its constructor parameters. Keep the implementation and runtime behavior unchanged.

Main handles startup, input parsing, command dispatch, and output framing in one method, which makes the control flow harder to read and maintain.\n\nSeparate the command loop from command dispatch and use an explicit switch with a default case. Keep each method at one logical level while preserving the existing command behavior.

The event confirmation line exceeds the project's 120-character readability limit, making the surrounding output code harder to scan.\n\nWrap the format call at natural argument boundaries without changing the rendered event message.

commitResults.messageBody: Introduce TaskList as the owner of the application task collection and its basic operations. Update Main to depend on the abstraction while preserving command processing, persistence, and console output behavior.
Move task-file loading, saving, serialization, and reconstruction into Storage. Keep Main focused on command flow while preserving the existing file format and user-facing error messages.

Introduce Parser to split console input into a command keyword and argument text. Update Main to consume ParsedCommand values while preserving command validation, task-number errors, and console output.

Move console input, startup and goodbye messages, generic error handling, and response separators into Ui. Keep task-specific command output in Main so this increment preserves behavior while reducing Main's responsibility for direct console interaction.

Centralize task list rendering and task-related confirmations in Ui. Keep Main focused on command validation and state changes while preserving the existing console output for additions, deletions, and status updates.

Give Main ownership of Ui, Storage, Parser, and TaskList through private fields. Move startup loading into the constructor and command-loop execution into run so the application lifecycle matches the extracted component design while preserving the existing entry point.

Move command dispatch, task creation, deletion, status updates, validation, and command error handling into CommandHandler. Keep Main focused on application setup, input parsing, and lifecycle control so its responsibilities remain minimal.

Add the abstract Command contract and migrate bye and list to ExitCommand and ListCommand. Keep the remaining command paths in CommandHandler so the stretch goal can be adopted incrementally without changing behavior.

Move todo, deadline, and event creation into command classes that share AddCommand behavior for updating, saving, and displaying tasks. Keep command handling incremental while preserving existing validation and output.

Move delete, mark, and unmark behavior into command classes and share task-number validation through TaskIndexCommand. Keep CommandHandler focused on command selection while preserving existing validation, persistence, and console output.

Make Parser construct concrete Command objects so command selection no longer lives in CommandHandler. Keep execution and error reporting behavior intact, and ensure bye stops processing subsequent input.

Remove the temporary CommandHandler adapter and let Main coordinate parsing, execution, error reporting, and exit handling. Keep the application state in Main so the command classes receive the same task list, UI, and storage components.
Parse new deadline values in yyyy-MM-dd format and display them as MMM dd yyyy. Persist typed dates in ISO form while preserving older free-text deadlines so existing task files remain loadable.
Extend typed deadlines to accept yyyy-MM-dd HHmm values while retaining date-only deadlines and legacy free-text loading. Format date-time deadlines for users and verify persistence across sessions.

Parse event boundaries as typed dates or date-times and format them consistently in the UI. Share date-time parsing and storage logic across deadlines and events while preserving legacy free-text event values.

Let users find typed deadlines and events occurring on a specified date. Use task-level date matching so date ranges remain encapsulated in the task classes, and keep legacy free-text tasks backward compatible.
Let users search task descriptions with the find command. Match keywords without regard to letter case, preserve task order, and show a clear response when no descriptions match.

Add JavaDoc to public classes, methods, task overrides, command implementations, and non-trivial helpers. Document explicit constructors so JavaDoc generation completes without warnings while preserving runtime behavior.
Replace the starter documentation with a concise guide covering setup, every supported command, date and time formats, persistence, examples, and common input mistakes.
Replace the project-template README with the Dr. Pijon guide so setup instructions and all supported commands are available from the repository root as well as the docs directory.
Add the three-step workflow for running a packaged JAR from an empty folder to both the root and docs user guides, including the Duke.jar example.
Explain where Gradle writes the packaged JAR and show the exact command to run it from the folder containing the copied file. Keep the instructions synchronized in the root and docs guides.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document JAR build and run workflow
commitResults.messageBody: Describe how to build the packaged JAR from the project root, where Gradle writes it, and how to run it from a folder containing the copied JAR. Keep the root and published guides synchronized.
Check the exit state before asking the scanner for another line so an interactive session does not wait for a second input after bye. Update the UI plan with a single-bye regression case.
Describe the purpose of application collaborators, command arguments, task data, date formatters, storage state, and UI fields. Improve maintainability while preserving runtime behavior.
